clue.text: (& 8dn.) King Charles casually poaches English premier gardener – she'll no doubt blame the Tories (6)

definitions.text: she'll no doubt blame the Tories

indicators.note: treated casually, the letters of Charles fall into a looser order
to poach is to take something in, so the scrambled name takes the next letters inside it

blocks.note: CHARLES rearranged; its S stays at the end to close round the inserted letters
Eve, one of the first pair tending the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: King Charles the keen gardener pinching the Chancellor, who blames every problem on the previous government.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Reeves is the Labour Chancellor of the Exchequer, fond of blaming the Conservatives' legacy. The answer runs on into 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeves, as Labour Chancellor, routinely attributes the country's financial problems to the previous Tory government.

clue.text: Doctor, I had sex, needing only half of my erectile state (8)

indicators.note: only half of the two-letter word MY is kept

blocks.note: to doctor results is to rig them
IT is a familiar word for sex

explanation.surface: A patient confessing to the doctor about a sex life and a condition only half there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person being addressed, but it is a verb meaning falsify. I'D comes straight from 'I had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity is stiffness, which is what an erection amounts to.

clue.text: see 18dn. (5)
Need scoop desperately? Here's a means of invading privacy (9)

indicators.note: done desperately, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tabloid hack desperate for a story, turning to phone-hacking or other snooping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about press intrusion; the definition is a joke, since an endoscope literally goes into the body's private places.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a camera tube passed inside the body, so it literally invades the privates.

clue.text: Lover-boy Macron, disconcerted, about to change direction (8)

indicators.note: thrown into confusion, the letters of Macron are jumbled
RE turns round to run the other way

explanation.surface: President Macron, cast as a flustered lover, about to switch his political course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to change direction' reads as Macron on the verge of a policy U-turn; it is RE followed by an instruction to reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer is someone who woos, a lover-boy.

clue.text: Ham's finished at function (7)

blocks.note: when something is finished it is over
to function is to act, operate

explanation.surface: A leftover ham finished off at a party or reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' reads as cold meat at a buffet, but it is a verb: to ham is to overplay a role. 'Function' is likewise a verb, not a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ham is to play a part with exaggerated, theatrical excess.

clue.text: "Kamala-Trump ends with lap dancing!" shock (5)

indicators.note: take only the end letters of Kamala and Trump
the letters of lap move about, as dancers do

explanation.surface: A scandal-sheet headline about the US presidential contest ending in a lap dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Kamala Harris and Donald Trump were rivals in the 2024 US election; the quoted headline is itself the shocking thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to fill someone with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Mark's erect, able to screw (9)

indicators.note: screwed up, the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A bloke called Mark boasting he is up for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name but is the verb, as in marking an anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of observing an occasion, as in marking a birthday.

clue.text: see 1ac.
US haircut given by doctor, an aggressive sort (6)

blocks.note: a hawk is one who favours force, as against a dove

explanation.surface: A spiky haircut handed out by a combative doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The US name for the crest of hair is Mohawk; British English usually calls it a Mohican, hence 'US'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohawk is the American name for a shaved head with a central crest.

clue.text: Pompous relative Ed is fussed about nothing (9)

indicators.note: fussed over, the letters of Ed is are rearranged
the rearranged letters go around the O

explanation.surface: A self-important relative called Ed making a fuss over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ed' reads as a man's name, but here it just supplies two letters to scramble with 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means pompous, pretentiously grand.

clue.text: Incredibly supple pensioner's initially missing a beat (5)

indicators.note: done incredibly, the letters are rearranged beyond belief
take the first letter of pensioner
that letter is removed from supple

blocks.note: first letter of pensioner, removed from SUPPLE to leave SUPLE

explanation.surface: An astonishingly flexible old-age pensioner who has lost his rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: One of SUPPLE's two Ps goes, and the remaining SUPLE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the throb felt at the wrist is a beat of the heart.

clue.text: Uniform: force needs to get rid of unflattering cap (5)

indicators.note: to get rid of something is to throw it out, so the letter is dropped from the word
a cap sits on top, so the first letter of unflattering

blocks.note: first letter of unflattering, removed from DURESS

explanation.surface: A police force that must ditch its unflattering hat as part of the uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like the police headgear but means the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress, as in mess dress or full dress, is a military uniform.

clue.text: One ball I've injured, with one wrapped on hand (9)

indicators.note: injured, the letters are knocked out of shape
one more A is taken into the mix

explanation.surface: A man with a hurt testicle, bandaged up while in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'one's become A, and all nine letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is on hand can be had or used right now.

clue.text: Heap of grass gives tense American a hit (7)

blocks.note: to sock someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A pile of cannabis leaves an edgy American a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' and 'hit' suggest drugs; grass is literal here and a hit is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a dense clump or mound of grass.

clue.text: Number two's prompted by its relaxation (9)

definitions.text: Number two's prompted by its relaxation

blocks.note: reads as a deputy, but 'number two' is nursery slang for a bowel movement
the bodily ring muscle that lets it out does so only when it loosens

explanation.surface: A deputy, the number two, spurred into action by some downtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' reads as a second-in-command, but it is nursery slang for defecation.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxing the anal sphincter is what lets a bowel movement happen.

clue.text: Italian's nutsack strained after getting end away (6)

indicators.note: strained, the letters are pulled out of shape
the end letter, K, is removed

blocks.note: last letter of nutsack, removed to leave NUTSAC

explanation.surface: An Italian man's scrotum under strain after getting his end away, slang for having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone from Tuscany, the region round Florence, is one kind of Italian.

clue.text: Maybe Georgia fell about somewhere in the palace? (9)

indicators.note: Georgia is just one example of the class STATE
to turn about is to face the other way, so MOOR is read backwards

blocks.note: a fell is upland moor, in northern England

explanation.surface: A woman called Georgia taking a tumble somewhere in a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the northern English noun for a hill moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Staterooms are the grand ceremonial rooms of a palace.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Poll turnover article by Hunt – get on with it! (3,2,3)

blocks.note: to poll is to cut off the hair or horns
T/O is the business abbreviation for turnover

explanation.surface: A pollster's figures on voter churn and an article by a politician named Hunt, with an impatient reader urging haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' and 'Hunt' dress up as an election survey and Jeremy Hunt, the Conservative politician, but they are plain verbs here. The answer runs on into 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from old films, which were told to skip the dialogue and go to the chase scene: stop dithering.

clue.text: Starmer welcomes start of honeymoon stage with cool indifference (6)

indicators.note: PM takes the following letters in
take the first letter of honeymoon

blocks.note: a leg of a journey is a stage

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's early honeymoon period with the voters being met with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: Starmer is Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister from 2024; the 'honeymoon stage' sounds like his early days in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm in its old sense is calm composure, stolid indifference.

clue.text: Miserable Cameron on being replaced by a bastard: "Grim" (7)

indicators.note: made miserable, the letters are left in disorder
when one thing is replaced by another, it goes and the other takes its place, so ON is swapped out for A and B

blocks.note: B is a standard abbreviation for bastard

explanation.surface: A gloomy David Cameron, ousted and replaced by a scoundrel, and the verdict is grim.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMERON loses ON and gains A and B, giving CAMERAB, which is then rearranged. David Cameron is a former Conservative Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something gruesome and death-haunted.

clue.text: House's continental cat piss (7)

indicators.note: both following words go into French, the language of the Continent

blocks.note: French for water, and piss is water in slang

explanation.surface: A European house that reeks of cat urine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' governs both words: the cat and the water are both in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French country house.

clue.text: Minister's arse tucked in (6)

blocks.note: both are insults for a contemptible man
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: A government minister whose backside has been tucked in, perhaps into tight trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked in' suggests one piece going inside another, but it is just the verb for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a curate is an assistant clergyman, one kind of minister of religion.

clue.text: Labour's elite ultimately wanting to get in a newspaper (6)

to get in is to enter, so FOR goes into the newspaper's letters

blocks.note: if you are for something you want it

explanation.surface: The Labour Party's top brass angling for coverage in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' reads as the party, but it is the plain noun for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for work or exertion, as in labour of love.

clue.text: Fellow with one ball, right erotic performer (9)

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' is the British swear word in the surface, but literally it means carrying blood. RTA, road traffic accident, is British police and hospital jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: With leader changed, scrap crew (5)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

blocks.note: a scrap is a fight; its F becomes E

clue.text: Good omen, sacked proprietor (5)

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's mock proprietor.

clue.text: Being comparatively sexy, not hard to be a fish-eater (5)

indicators.note: 'not hard' tells you the result has no hard in it, so the H goes

explanation.definitionFit: Otters live largely on fish.

clue.text: Bully is next to introduce rate change (8)
